Red Team Operation Methodology.description: Full red team operation checklist — from planning and C2 setup through post-op reporting. Covers OPSEC, infrastructure, and rules of engagement.

steps.task: Obtain signed Rules of Engagement (RoE) document before any activity
Define scope — in-scope IPs, domains, accounts, physical locations
Define out-of-scope — production systems, payment systems, specific users
Establish emergency contact / deconfliction process with blue team
Define success criteria and objectives (DA? Data exfil? Physical access?)
Agree on operation timeline and reporting cadence
Establish safe words / emergency stop procedure
Acquire dedicated VPS infrastructure — separate from personal/corporate IPs
Register lookalike domains with privacy WHOIS (>30 days old for category bypass)
Obtain valid SSL certificates for C2 domains (Let's Encrypt)
Set up redirectors — Nginx/Apache to forward only valid beacon traffic to C2
Configure CDN/domain fronting for HTTPS C2 traffic
Build malleable C2 profile mimicking legitimate traffic (O365, Teams, CDN)
Configure DNS C2 channel as backup (dnscat2 / Cobalt Strike DNS beacon)
Set up payload staging server (separate from C2) with HTTPS
Test all C2 channels before operation — verify callback and tasking works
Configure operator VPN and ensure all traffic routes through it
Social media C2 infrastructure — consider Discord (bot token) or Telegram (bot API) as covert C2 channels; traffic blends with legitimate HTTPS to known CDNs; use as out-of-band backup C2 only
Cloud storage C2 — configure C2 over legitimate cloud services (GitHub Gists, Azure Blob Storage, S3) to blend with normal business traffic; ensure content appears benign
NEVER use personal email, accounts, or home IP for any operation activity
Use dedicated attack VM — no crossover with personal tools or browsing
Clear artifact markers — change default tool signatures, UUIDs, user-agents
Operate within target's business hours to blend with normal user activity
Use target-appropriate LOLBins — avoid dropping offensive tooling when possible
Test payloads against sandboxes before deploying (Any.run, Hybrid Analysis)
Randomize sleep/jitter on beacons — avoid fixed-interval callbacks
Do NOT scan the entire internet or run aggressive tools without need
Keep detailed operation log with timestamps for all actions taken
Back up all loot/evidence to operator-controlled storage immediately
Avoid EDR telemetry — use PPID spoofing, indirect syscalls, and in-memory execution; avoid writing payloads to disk; use process hollowing into signed binaries
API call pattern discipline — space out cloud API calls; avoid rapid enumeration that triggers anomaly detection; mimic legitimate access patterns in volume and timing
External recon — Shodan, Censys, Subfinder, theHarvester, GitHub secrets
Phishing campaign setup — GoPhish / evilginx2 with RoE-approved pretext
Payload generation — AV-bypassed beacon, test before sending
Exploit external service if in scope (CVE-validated, not destructive)
Physical access attempt if in scope — tailgating, BadUSB, rogue AP
Verify initial foothold — confirm callback, user context, and connectivity
Situational awareness — whoami, systeminfo, network config, AV/EDR
Establish persistence (only if in scope) — scheduled task / registry / service
Credential harvesting — Mimikatz, LaZagne, credential file hunting
Internal network recon — BloodHound, nmap via SOCKS proxy
Privilege escalation to local admin or domain user
Lateral movement to additional hosts — PtH, PtT, WMI, WinRM
Escalate to Domain Admin via identified attack path
Demonstrate objective — DCSync, access target data, reach critical system
Identify 'crown jewel' data as defined in RoE — do NOT exfil real PII/secrets
Create canary file to prove access without touching real sensitive data
Demonstrate exfil channel — DNS tunnel, HTTPS C2, cloud storage
Document what could have been taken and estimated data volume
Remove all payloads, backdoors, and artifacts created during operation
Restore any modified files or registry keys to original state
Confirm with client that all implants are removed
Write executive summary — business impact, key findings, risk level
Write technical report — full attack chain, TTPs mapped to MITRE ATT&CK
Include screenshots and logs proving each step of attack chain
Provide remediation recommendations for every finding
Present findings to client — walk through attack chain, answer questions
Securely delete all client data from operator systems
